title: Rabbi Chalafta (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: One of the five sons of Rabbi Yose, as stated explicitly in the Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Yevamot, and Shabbat 118b: Rabbi Yose performed levirate marriage with the wife of his brother who had died, and she bore him five sons. In Midrash Tehillim 100:2: “Rabbi Simon and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi in the name of Rabbi Chalafta” (and Hyman suggests that possibly this is this Rabbi Chalafta): “A mortal king, when [a person] confesses, gives him to the executioner — but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so,” etc. Yuchasin wrote that he died in his father’s lifetime, from Semachot, chapter 10, but Hyman does not find it there; in Moed Katan 21a only an incident is mentioned in which Rabbi Yose’s son died in Tzippori, and his name is not mentioned. In the entry Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta Hyman explains that he was the son of this Rabbi Chalafta.

notes.text: The possible Chalafta identification, negative observation about Semachot and proposed son Shimon are Hyman’s. בן בנו is grandson; the five-son family and unnamed death report are not collapsed into an independently established identity.

The consulted Shabbat 118b directly lists Chalafta among Rabbi Yose’s five sons; its discussion continues by qualifying the statement about five acts of intercourse. That scalar does not itself state Hyman’s levirate-marriage account. The possible Midrash Tehillim Chalafta identification, unnamed death notice and Shimon genealogy remain Hyman’s account; a named parallel is not identity admission.
